newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait bourse ends record week up 4.6 precent.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait bourse ends record week up 4.6 precent.

text.p: A strong performance on the Kuwait Stock Exchange in the week to Wednesday revived warnings by some analysts of a possible correction.
"Exaggerated trading is dangerous," said leading Kuwaiti economist Jassem al-Saddoun of trading value in Wednesday's session which reached 118.3 million dinars ($391 million).
The KSE index, which set new highs over the past three days, ended the week up 107 points at a record 2,439.9 points. It rose 19.9 points on Wednesday.
"The higher the index goes the bigger the correction will be and the more painful," said Saddoun.
KSE head Hisham al-Oteibi told Reuters on Wednesday that corrections were normal although he said the strong performance could continue.

Warnings of a crash by parliamentarians and of a correction by economists emerged earlier this month after the index reached 2,354.7 points on April 27. In late April, trading value on the KSE soared to a record 125.8 million dinars during a single 2-1/2-hour session in which 445 million shares were traded.

Daily trading value grew during the week reaching 118.3 million dinars on Wednesday from 81.7 million the previous day and 72.4 million on Monday. The daily average for the week to last Wednesday was 39 million dinars.
Trading volume on Wednesday reached 420 million shares from an average 300 million shares changing hands a day over the past two days. Last week's daily average was 134 million.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest in mutual funds.
